newsitem.title: USA: FCC to ok licenses for 15 next-gen satellites - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: FCC to ok licenses for 15 next-gen satellites - WSJ.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission could issue licenses for 15 next-generation satellite systems as soon as April, the Wall Street Journal said Tuesday.

The licenses will let applicants determine if they can find financial backing to build the systems, which would be deployed beginning in the year 2000 and cost a total of $23 billion, the report said.
Applicants include PanAmSat, Lockheed Martin Corp, AT&T, a Motorola subsidiary and a unit of General Electric, the report said.

Don Gips, chief of the FCC's international bureau, told the paper it might take longer to issue licenses for the new high-bandwith systems that would allow high-speed Internet communication or complex video and data transmissions.
